text:
Plugins, agents, and skills for AI coding tools

 
 

Use one collection of plugins, agents, skills, and commands across Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, Antigravity CLI, GitHub Copilot, and Pi. A harness is the coding tool that loads and runs the components.

Contributors write each component once, in Markdown, in the Claude Code plugin format. Adapters under tools/adapters/ generate the format each harness reads, map model aliases to that harness's models, and translate tool permissions where the harness supports them. CI regenerates the artifacts for every harness, validates them, and runs the OpenCode, Antigravity CLI, and Pi artifacts through their installed CLIs. The capability matrix lists what each harness supports, and ARCHITECTURE.md describes the design.

The catalog contains 93 plugins, including 91 local plugins and 2 external entries. The local source contains 199 agents, 185 skills, and 103 commands. Plugins cover Python and JavaScript development, code review, testing, infrastructure, security, and other work.

 Multi-harness support

Choose the harness you use and follow its setup route. Available components depend on the installation route and the harness's capabilities.

 Tool Installation Components and limits 
 --- --- --- 
 Claude Code Plugin marketplace Source agents, skills, and commands; plugin-specific hooks and MCP configuration 
 OpenAI Codex CLI Native marketplace or generated artifacts Native source skills; generated TOML agents and commands as skills use a separate route 
 Cursor Plugin marketplace Source agents, skills, and commands, with curated project rules 
 OpenCode make install-opencode Generated agents, skills, and commands, with translated tool permissions 
 Antigravity CLI make install-antigravity Generated plugins containing agents, skills, and commands 
 GitHub Copilot make install-copilot Generated agent profiles and skills; commands also become invocable skills 
 Pi make install-pi Generated skills and prompt templates; agents require a subagent extension 

See the capability matrix for model mappings, tool permissions, hooks, and installation differences.

For individual skills, use a skills-only installer and select your coding tool.

 How it works

A plugin groups related agents, skills, and commands under plugins/ . For example, python-development contains three agents, sixteen skills, and a scaffolding command. The chosen harness loads the installed components according to its own discovery and invocation rules.

Contributors maintain one Markdown source in the Claude Code plugin format. Native registries point to that source where supported, and adapters generate the formats needed by each harness. Commands may become skills or prompt templates, and agent formats, model choices, and tool permissions vary by harness.

Source agents specify model aliases such as opus , sonnet , haiku , fable , or inherit . Adapters map those aliases to each harness's model settings, including fixed defaults for some inherit entries. See model configuration and the adapter mappings.

 Quality evaluation

The repository validates plugin structure, generated artifacts, and documentation. Contributors can run these checks from the repository root:

 

 plugin-eval also provides static skill checks without model calls. For example:

 

The LLM judge and Monte Carlo layers are experimental and are not validated against human labels. Their scores describe model assessments and repeated simulations and do not prove that a task succeeds in a project. They require the optional llm dependencies. Model calls use ANTHROPIC API KEY when it is set and bill that API account. Otherwise they use your Claude Code login. See the evaluation guide for setup and limits.

 Quick start

Choose a plugin for the work you do:

 Plugin Use it for 
 --- --- 
 python-development Python, Django, FastAPI, testing, and packaging 
 javascript-typescript JavaScript and TypeScript development and project setup 
 developer-essentials Code review, debugging, Git, and testing patterns 
 security-scanning Security review, dependency checks, and code scanning

Native installation also reads the original skill bodies, while generated copies split oversized bodies into reference files for the 8 KB budget. See the Codex setup details before choosing an installation route.

 Cursor

Cursor uses the committed plugin marketplace registry. Follow the Cursor setup instructions to add the marketplace and install a plugin.

 
 

 Skills only

Install an individual skill with GitHub CLI's gh skill command or the npx skills installer. Select your coding tool when prompted. Both installers read skills from GitHub without cloning the repository and install them without the plugin's agents, commands, or hooks.

 

 gh skill requires GitHub CLI 2.90 or later. The npx command requires Node.js and npm. See skills-only installation for other agents, install scopes, and version pinning.

install.html:
Choose a plugin for the work you do:

Plugin Use it for
python-development Python, Django, FastAPI, testing, and packaging
javascript-typescript JavaScript and TypeScript development and project setup
developer-essentials Code review, debugging, Git, and testing patterns
security-scanning Security review, dependency checks, and code scanning

See the plugin catalog for all 93 plugins and the usage guide for commands and examples.

Claude Code

Run these commands inside Claude Code to register the marketplace and install the Python development plugin:

/plugin marketplace add wshobson/agents
/plugin install python-development@claude-code-workflows

Then ask Claude to use the Python agents for your task, or run the plugin's scaffolding command:

/python-development:python-scaffold Create a FastAPI service with tests
Codex CLI

Run these commands in a terminal with a current Codex CLI:

codex plugin marketplace add wshobson/agents
codex plugin add python-development@claude-code-workflows

The native Codex manifests expose source skills. The generated TOML agents and command-derived skills use a separate adapter path. Native installation also reads the original skill bodies, while generated copies split oversized bodies into reference files for the 8 KB budget. See the Codex setup details before choosing an installation route.

Cursor

Cursor uses the committed plugin marketplace registry. Follow the Cursor setup instructions to add the marketplace and install a plugin.

Skills only

Install an individual skill with GitHub CLI's gh skill command or the npx skills installer. Select your coding tool when prompted. Both installers read skills from GitHub without cloning the repository and install them without the plugin's agents, commands, or hooks.

gh skill install wshobson/agents python-testing-patterns
npx skills add wshobson/agents --skill python-testing-patterns

gh skill requires GitHub CLI 2.90 or later. The npx command requires Node.js and npm. See skills-only installation for other agents, install scopes, and version pinning.

Install from a clone

For OpenCode, Antigravity CLI, GitHub Copilot, and Pi, clone the repository and use the installer for your harness. Install uv, Python 3.12 or later, and the coding tool you want to use. The following clone command uses GitHub CLI:

gh repo clone wshobson/agents ~/agents
cd ~/agents

Run the command for your tool. Each target generates the artifacts and links all local plugins into that tool's user configuration:

make install-opencode
make install-antigravity
make install-copilot
make install-pi

Pi's agents require its reference subagent extension or a compatible extension. See the global install guide for configuration paths and uninstall commands.
